_comment: Reference shape of one gateway cron job as reported by `openclaw cron list --json` (OpenClaw 2026.10.x). The job store is gateway-owned and SQLite-backed: do not hand-edit files under ~/.openclaw/cron/. Create jobs with `openclaw cron add` (see _create_comment) and read them back with `openclaw cron list --json`. Replace every <ANGLE_BRACKETS> placeholder.
_create_comment: openclaw cron add --name <short-id> --description '<one-line description>' --cron '0 7 * * *' --tz <IANA/Timezone> --session isolated --model <provider>/<model> --thinking low --timeout-seconds 600 --tools exec,read --message 'Run /path/to/your/script.sh and post the result.' --announce --channel <channel-plugin-id> --to <channel-type>:<channel-id>
name: <short-id>
_schedule_comment: Standard 5-field cron syntax. Always set tz; the default is the gateway host clock.
_sessionTarget_comment: isolated runs in a fresh session. current posts into the session that created the job.
_payload_comment: Pin the model and thinking level per job; there is no shared :cron alias. Keep toolsAllow minimal: every exposed tool schema adds input tokens to every run. Pass it with --tools at creation; omitting --tools stores *, which gives the job the owner session's full tool policy. Reference a script file instead of composing shell in the message.
_delivery_comment: Always set an explicit channel and target. A bare announce with several channels configured can land in the wrong one.
